about: World answer key rule changes and what each one touches (KPC owner, 2026-11-11). Part of the world rules hash. Same format as .github/us-key-rule-scope.json; the areas are country codes. The world key has no per-country rules rows yet, so a change that says all (or lists nothing) rebuilds every country on the next run.

changes.why: A layer that fails with no saved records no longer holds its country: the parks the previous key joined through it keep their previous entry and the rest is rebuilt (logged, listed as fell_back in the key file). A saved copy's records from a layer the country no longer reads are not counted or brought back. decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-11.

France reads three more PatriNat layers from the IGN Géoplateforme WFS it already reads the ZNIEFF layers from: marine ZNIEFF type II (patrinat_znieff2_mer), Conservatoire du littoral sites (patrinat_cdl) and the protection perimeters of national nature reserves (patrinat_pprnn); only France reads them. With them, the saved-outline step judges a park by the pieces W-2 keeps (the agency pieces when a park also has EEA pieces), so a park joined to an agency WFS record and its EEA copy gets a saved outline the page can draw. That step runs for every country, so the scope is all; no join changes outside France. decided_by KPC owner, 2026-11-11.

D6, tables out of the rule scripts (KPC owner, 2026-11-12): the per-country tables (built-in sources SRC with the EEA layers of each EU country, the EU list, GEN, LOC, KINDS, SIDE_NOT, the Swiss type preference, the Queensland split layers) move, unchanged, from kpc_world_key.py into data/world-key/area-tables.json, read at start (fail closed on a missing or malformed file); the saved copy's date is the one run date (KPC_BUILD_DATE, else today read once). No result changes: the loaded tables equal the old ones (SRC in the same order), and the builder gives byte-identical key files before and after on the same saved copy (tests/test_area_tables_nov12.py). So no country is rebuilt for it; an area-hash add run rebuilds every country once (the D7 run).

Official pin fills (kpc_pin_fill.py; KPC-Data data/intake/official-pins-nov12.json, the pin-fill rows marked ready): a park POTA has no usable pin for (absent or 0,0) is joined by its official pin and marked pf; a POTA pin is never moved and a fill is ignored once POTA has a usable pin. The ready world fills are PF-0033 and PF-0034 (French Polynesia) and AU-10111 (Australia, on the signed expected-hold list: it waits until AU is built again), so only PF and AU results change.

The world builder can read the Japan A10 crosswalk (data/research-inbox/answers/nov5/JP_A10_crosswalk.csv, kpc_jp_crosswalk.py) as official Japanese name aliases for JP parks, behind the repo variable KPC_JP_A10_CROSSWALK. The switch stays OFF until the owner signs the Japan A10 licence terms; OFF, the file is not read and every country's result is byte for byte what it was, so no country is due for this change. Turning the switch on changes JP only (that is a variable, not a code change: the JP area hash must count it).

Quality must-fix M2: kpc_pin_fill.py and kpc_jp_crosswalk.py are in the world RULE_FILES (removed from NOT_RULES). A later edit to either file moves the world hash. No join result changes (the builders already called them; the Japan switch stays off); no country is rebuilt for this alone.

Owner hold of CA-2241, CA-1974 and CA-1997 in kpc_pin_fill.py (Quality, delegated by Brandon 4:43 AM CT). The file is in the world RULE_FILES so this edit moves the world hash; no world country result changes (the new holds are Canada refs; PF-0033/34 stay held; the AU fill still applies), so no country is rebuilt.
